prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Generate ONE bitmap that looks exactly like an ordinary captured frame of a running, implementable 2D pixel-art Chinese cultivation action RPG, NOT promotional art or concept art. Landscape 16:9. Topic: jade-green Chinese mountain cultivation setting, a cultivator actively casting a jade water spell toward a wooden training dummy in a small temple courtyard.

CRITICAL RENDERING CONTRACT:
Treat the entire game as a native 384 x 216 pixel framebuffer, enlarged 4x with nearest-neighbor. Visibly chunky square pixels everywhere, one consistent pixel size throughout the environment, character, UI and magic. Only about 24-32 flat palette colors in total: dark ink teal outlines, four jade/teal ramp colors, four gray-blue stone ramp colors, muted moss greens, ivory, cinnabar and restrained amber accents. NO smooth gradients, NO antialiasing, NO photoreal texture, NO brushwork, NO 3D render, NO depth-of-field, NO bokeh, NO volumetric light, NO cinematic perspective or lens effects. Limit shading to two or three clearly stepped solid colors per material. Do not make the background more detailed or differently lit than the sprites. It must look like ONE coherent handcrafted pixel game, not a pixel character pasted onto a realistic painting.

GAME CAMERA AND ASSET BUDGET:
Fixed orthographic top-down three-quarter RPG camera, comparable to a practical tile-based overhead adventure game. Floor is a legible repeating grid of 16x16 native-pixel stone tiles, a small number of reusable chipped tile variations, no complex decorative carved floor. Playable rectangular courtyard occupies the central 65 percent of the image. Simple waist-high tiled parapet, a modest traditional temple roof along the upper edge, two repeated stone lantern sprites, clusters of moss and two small pine trees. Mountain silhouettes and a thin cloud layer visible beyond the parapet in the top background, only three flat parallax layers. Keep scenery sparse and readable, with traversable empty space and visible arena edges. No enormous vista, no spectacular architecture, no waterfalls, no hundreds of objects.
Main character: a SMALL 20x28 native-pixel humanoid sprite with a readable white robe, red sash, black hair, teal shadow and 1-pixel dark outline; face indicated by only 2-3 pixels. Keep the sprite grounded to the tile floor with a simple dark oval shadow. Other scenery uses the same outline, lighting and pixel scale.
Training dummy: 18x26 native-pixel sprite, same scale and outline rules, with a short health bar.
Spell: mid-cast. A short curved jade wave crescent traveling from the hero to the dummy, built from three nested flat-color jagged pixel shapes. About 55x28 native pixels total, plus only 12 square water motes, three small trailing afterimage shapes and a tiny impact star. This spell should be straightforward to reproduce as a few sprite frames and particle rectangles. NOT a giant dragon or intricate magical illustration.

COMPOSITION:
Hero stands a little left of center, dummy to right, clear spell direction left to right, three-quarter overhead angle. Foreground paving is partially occluded by a simple low wall at the very bottom. Small restrained game HUD: upper-left tiny character portrait square, red HP bar and teal energy bar, top-right a simple boxed minimap with a few tile marks and an amber player dot; bottom center four small bordered ability slots with simple pixel pictograms and key labels 1 2 3 4. No decorative UI frames, no large title, no promotional typography, no caption, no watermark. These HUD elements use the SAME low-resolution pixel grid. An understated tiny damage number 128 just above the dummy is acceptable.
Art direction: restrained attractive nostalgic 16-bit Chinese fantasy, stronger chunky pixel character coherence like a real indie game screenshot, production-feasible sprite and tile set, not polished HD illustration. Prioritize consistent pixel-grid construction, gameplay readability and implementability over richness.
note: Generated visual reference, not an actual running game screenshot. Native resolution and palette in the prompt are design targets, not verified properties of the generated image.
